what: DSP 3.0.13's own DTMF, generated inside the emulator by the C52 firmware and captured off its line output
image: IDSDL302.ROM (supervisor + DSP 3.0.13, 20.16 MHz), booted through the captured on-chip ROM

files.line-tx.s16le: the raw signed 16-bit little-endian samples --dsp-tx-pcm wrote

sample_rate_basis: the DSP's codec rate for the dial path (docs/codec-rate-312.md); the bursts decode as the dialed digits at 7200 Hz and as nothing sensible at 9600 Hz, and the bridge's own 7200->9600 conversion is what the exchange decoded from
why_it_is_audible: the idsdl302 NVRAM fixture now carries the +S block, so the dial path sends +S22/+S24/+S26 = 020d/32c8/0c08 on tags 0x19/0x1a/0x1b; with the block erased the lanes carry ffff and the same run produces no decodable tone (docs/idsdl-extended-registers.md)
caveats: Synthetic line generation is off whenever the exchange is attached, so only the C52 program could have produced these samples; but the codec, ASIC transport and line are models.
The 7200 Hz rate is the firmware's dial-path rate as inferred from its phase increments, not a measurement of the board's codec clock.
Tone and gap timing come from the supervisor's own S11 countdown paced by the emulator tick, not from measured hardware timing.
